DDS.definition: Digital Dealership System (DDS) is a dealership management platform designed for automotive businesses to manage sales deals, employees, stores, and customer data. It provides insights, reports, and analytics across multiple dealerships.

Stores.definition: Each dealership or branch location. Reports and permissions are store-specific.

Employees.definition: DDS tracks employees (salespersons, managers, finance, etc.). Only active employees (not disabled) are included in reports. Permissions determine what data each employee can see.

Deals.definition: A record of a car sale created in the sales_deals table. Deals capture vehicle details, sales, gross, and salespersons. They can be filtered by date ranges like Today, MTD, YTD, Last Month, etc.

Permissions.definition: System-specific access rights that decide what a user can see or do. A user linked to a store may only see deals relevant to that store.

Settings.definition: Dealer-specific configurations applied to database queries along with time filters.

Reports.definition: DDS provides reporting features such as sales performance by employee, store comparisons, gross reports, pacing reports, and trends.

Salesperson.definition: An employee assigned to a sales deal. If a deal has salespersonId filled, that employee is considered a Salesperson.A salesperson is responsible for selling cars to customers. Their performance is measured by units sold (new, used), gross profit (frontend, backend), and trends (MTD, YTD, etc.).

SalesManager.definition: An employee assigned to a sales deal. If a deal has salesmanagerId filled, that employee is considered a Sales manager.A sales manager oversees the sales team and dealership performance. Their metrics include total units managed, gross profit contribution, and team trends. They may also handle wholesale and oversee salesperson performance.

FinanceManager.definition: An employee assigned to a sales deal. If a deal has finance manager Id filled, that employee is considered a Finance manager.A finance manager arranges financing and insurance products for customers. Their performance is measured by units financed, gross profit from backend finance products, and contribution to overall dealership profitability.

Brand.definition: Brand performance data represents sales performance segmented by manufacturer or car brand (Toyota, Honda, etc.). It shows how different brands are performing within the dealership.

CSI.definition: Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) is a score that measures customer satisfaction, often collected through surveys. Higher CSI indicates better service quality.

Pace.definition: A metric used to compare sales progress against previous trends or expected performance.

Trends.definition: Comparison of sales numbers over different durations (e.g., MTD vs LMTD, YTD vs LYTD).

DDSQueryLogic.definition: Always apply dealership settings + permissions + active employees filter + correct time duration when fetching data.

Units.definition: Units are all cars or a vehicle that are being sold in the system

New Units.definition: Units are all new cars or a vehicle that are being sold in the system

Used Units.definition: Units are all used cars or a vehicle that are being sold in the system

Trade Units.definition: Units are traded cars or a vehicle that are being sold in trade of other vehicle

Sales.definition: Total revenue generated from all deals before any deductions. (Previously called Gross Sales)
Sales.formula: Sales = Total Revenue from all deals

Gross.definition: Earnings remaining after deducting costs (Previously called Net).

Today.formula: Today = SUM(Deals where date = current date)

MTD.definition: Month-to-Date, from the 1st day of the current month until today.
MTD.formula: MTD = SUM(Deals from 1st of current month to today)

YTD.definition: Year-to-Date, from January 1st of the current year until today.
YTD.formula: YTD = SUM(Deals from Jan 1st of current year to today)

LM.definition: Last Month, data from the entire previous month.
LM.formula: LM = SUM(Deals from 1st to last day of previous month)

LMTD.definition: Last Month Till Date, from the 1st to the current/today date of the previous month.
LMTD.formula: LMTD = SUM(Deals from 1st of previous month to current/today date)

LYTD.definition: Last Year Till Date, from January 1st to the current/today date of the previous year.
LYTD.formula: LYTD = SUM(Deals from Jan 1st of previous year to current/today date)

SameMonth.definition: MTD of the current year compared with the same month of the previous year.
SameMonth.formula: SameMonth = MTD(current year) vs MTD(previous year)
